newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO SELL 36.4 PCT OF ITS MINT.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO SELL 36.4 PCT OF ITS MINT.

text.p: Poland wants to offer 1,999,999 shares, or 36.4 percent, of its mint in a public offer, selling 1,499,999 existing shares and raising the firm's capital by a new issue of 500,000 shares, the government press office said.

Jerzy Izdebski of the press office said the government's economic committee (KERM) gave on Monday its go-ahead to the offer which would be divided into a small and large investor tranche and an employee tranche.

"After the privatisation the treasury will hold 50 percent or 2,750,001 shares of the mint, employees would have 750,000 shares or 13.6 percent and investors 1,999,999 shares or 36.4 percent of the company," Izdebski said.
He did not give any financial details of company saying only the firm was profitable though its earnings fell last year due to reduced orders from the National Bank of Poland.
Izdebski did not say when the privatisation would take place.
